entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Pope Marcellus I was the bishop of Rome from May or June 308 to his death on 16 January 309. He succeeded Marcellinus after a considerable interval. Under Maxentius, he was banished from Rome in 309, on account of the tumult caused by the severity of the penances he had imposed on Christians who had lapsed under the recent persecution. He died the same year, being succeeded by Eusebius. His relics are under the altar of San Marcello al Corso in Rome. Since 1969 his feast day, traditionally kept by the Catholic Church, commemorates his leadership during a tumultuous period in Roman history. The Edict of Milan, issued by Constantine in 313, would later influence the theological debates that Marcellus I navigated. The Arian controversy, sparked by the doctrine of Arianism, also played a significant role in Marcellus I's papacy. The Council of Nicaea, convened by Constantine in 325, would eventually settle the controversy, but during Marcellus I's tenure, the church was divided between Arian and orthodox factions. Marcellus I's papacy is notable for its short duration, yet the theological debates he faced would have lasting impacts on the development of Christian doctrine. The papacy of Marcellus I serves as a reminder of the complexities and challenges faced by early Christian leaders as they navigated the complexities of empire and theology.
